text:
morgan: Heads up — US-west3 batch provisioning is failing fast. GPU attach is hanging for ~30s, and i'm seeing local nvme iops pinned during attach windows. likely the scrub/cleaner cadence is colliding with batch launches.

raj: Ugh. Any obvious errors in node logs?

morgan: pasted quick tail from node (iostat + dmesg).
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200.0  3400.0  51200  450000     128.0     1.9   6.2    1.0     7.2   0.2  98.7
```
```
[ 1234.567890] scrubber[d]: start async scrub for /dev/nvme0n1
[ 1234.569000] nvme0n1: queue depth saturated, fallback throttle
[ 1235.001200] gpu-attach: device attach timeout waiting for ephemeral disk
```
```
kubectl describe pod gpu-attach-job-xx
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning AttachError  2m   kubelet            attach timed out: iops spike on /var/lib/kubelet/plugins
```

kelly: So scrub kicks right when we try to attach, and nvme %util shows saturation. Could be thermal or writeback backlog too.

sre-jen: Can we confirm if these nodes had any firmware/cleaner-rollout recently? Also region-wide or single cohort?

morgan: It's a cohort in us-west3-a, ~120 hosts. No firmware push in last 48h, but we did flip cleaner cadence from 00/30 -> dynamic two nights ago.

raj: Two prongs: 1) short-term mitigation: delay scruber on those cohorts during peak attach windows and add cpu/io niceness; 2) medium-term: tune cleaner to stagger and respect upcoming attach schedule from the scheduler.

kelly: Agree. Short-term patch: mark the cohort with label infra.skip-scrub=true via fleet-config and trigger a rolling pause for scrub housekeeping. I'd rather not disable all janitors.

morgan: I'm going to run a one-off tweak: set scrub window back to low-aggressiveness and set ioprio for scrub threads. Command i'll use: `fleetctl update-cohort us-west3-a --scrub-aggr=low --scrub-ioprio=5`

deploy-bot: [info] scrub-scheduler: scheduled dynamic scrub scaleback for cohort us-west3-a at 1728604800

raj: Also watch for residual writeback: run `echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`? hmm that's too blunt. Maybe run fsync/drain for leftover pods before attach.

kelly: Cost note — if we stagger less aggressively we'll increase scrub duration and temporary storage wear (more writes spread), but avoids attach failures that cause customer latency and lost GPU minutes. tradeoff: ~3% extra scrub IO for 12h vs 10-15% failed attach spike.

morgan: I'll roll the scrub scaleback now and monitor attach success rate. setting metrics alert to watch nvme_util and gpu_attach_latency.

sre-jen: If we still see high %util after scaleback, escalate to hardware team for thermal investigation. Also capture SMART counters: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` and upload to ops ticket.

morgan: will do. i'm also adding a short-lived scheduler policy: prefer older nodes for batch attaches while scrub is throttled. patching autoscaler to consider `ephemeral_quiet` label.

raj: Thanks. keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:

morgan: update — scrub scaleback applied at 1728604760. attach success rate jumped from 72% -> 98% in the first 5m. leaving monitoring on for 1h.

deploy-bot: [info] gpu-autoscaler: temporary attach-policy applied for cohort us-west3-a (prefer_quiet=true)

kelly: Nice. Followups: schedule postmortem to decide if cleaner cadence needs smarter backoff tied to attach forecasts, and estimate cost delta for expanded scrub windows.

morgan: agreed — creating a short RFC for scrub-scheduler and autoscaler tie-in. I'll ping infra-ops and sched-team.
